name: Agra
shortDescription: Home of the Taj Mahal, Agra also rewards time for its Mughal fort, garden tombs, river views and a living tradition of stone inlay craft.
description:
The Taj Mahal is reason enough to visit Agra, but treating the city as a single-monument photo stop misses the wider Mughal story. Agra Fort, Itimad-ud-Daulah, Mehtab Bagh and Akbar's tomb at Sikandra reveal successive generations of architecture and garden design.

Stay at least one night if possible. This creates a weather buffer, makes an early Taj visit easier and leaves time to see the fort without sprinting back to Delhi. Distances are manageable, though traffic around the monument zones can be slow.

Ticketing, weekly closures and security restrictions matter here. Carry only essential items to the Taj Mahal, use official ticket channels, and reconfirm current rules before your visit.
bestTimeToVisit:
October to March is generally the best period. November through February offers cooler walking weather, but winter fog can obscure morning views and disrupt trains. Keep a second viewing window if the Taj is the centre of the trip.

April to June is extremely hot. July to September brings humidity and monsoon showers, along with greener gardens and fewer visitors. Sunrise is cooler and often quieter in most seasons, subject to fog and current entry arrangements.
bestTimeToVisitShort: October to March; winter mornings may be foggy
budgetEstimate: ₹1,800–5,500 per person per day (excluding intercity travel)

topAttractions.name: Taj Mahal
topAttractions.description: Shah Jahan's marble mausoleum is best appreciated slowly: through the gateway reveal, garden axis, changing stone detail and Yamuna setting. Carry minimal belongings and verify the weekly closure and ticket rules.
topAttractions.timings: Closed Friday for general tourism; verify official hours
topAttractions.entryFee: Ticketed; mausoleum access may cost extra

topAttractions.name: Agra Fort
topAttractions.description: A vast red-sandstone imperial complex with palaces, audience halls and framed views toward the Taj Mahal. Allow two hours rather than treating it as an add-on.

topAttractions.name: Itimad-ud-Daulah
topAttractions.description: This refined garden tomb is often called the Baby Taj, but its delicate marble inlay and intimate scale deserve independent attention.

topAttractions.name: Mehtab Bagh
topAttractions.description: A riverside Mughal garden aligned with the Taj Mahal, popular for late-afternoon views from across the Yamuna.

topAttractions.name: Akbar's Tomb, Sikandra
topAttractions.description: The emperor's monumental tomb stands in a large enclosed garden northwest of central Agra and shows a different phase of Mughal design.

topAttractions.name: Fatehpur Sikri
topAttractions.description: Akbar's former imperial capital contains palaces, courts and the Jama Masjid about 40 kilometres from Agra. Plan it as a half-day excursion.

topAttractions.name: Chini ka Rauza
topAttractions.description: A quieter riverside tomb notable for surviving glazed-tile decoration. Its condition and surroundings are less polished than headline monuments.

topAttractions.name: Ram Bagh
topAttractions.description: One of India's earliest surviving Mughal gardens, offering a calmer look at the river landscape and garden tradition.

localFood.name: Agra Petha
localFood.description: A translucent ash-gourd sweet sold plain or flavoured; buy from a reputable shop and check packaging dates.
localFood.whereToTry: Established sweet shops in central Agra

localFood.name: Bedai and Aloo Sabzi
localFood.description: A crisp, spiced breakfast bread served with potato curry, often followed by jalebi.
localFood.whereToTry: Busy morning shops around the old city

localFood.name: Mughlai Korma
localFood.description: Slow-cooked meat or vegetable gravies reflect Agra's imperial culinary legacy.

localFood.name: Dalmoth
localFood.description: A savoury mixture of lentils, nuts and spices that travels well as a packaged snack.

localFood.name: Paratha
localFood.description: Stuffed flatbreads make a practical breakfast or lunch with yoghurt and pickle.

localFood.name: Jalebi
localFood.description: Fresh coils of crisp syrupy batter are commonly paired with Agra's savoury breakfast dishes.

tips: Verify official ticketing, closure and permitted-item rules before arrival.
Carry as little as possible because security checks are strict.
Keep weather flexibility in winter when fog may hide the monument.
Use prepaid, app-based or hotel-arranged transport and confirm the total fare.
Battery vehicles operate in restricted zones near the Taj.
Allow a half day for Fatehpur Sikri and do not accept unsolicited guiding services.
Use licensed guides and agree on duration and price first.
Buy stone inlay only from transparent sellers who document materials and shipping terms.
Taj East Gate is convenient for an early visit.
Fatehabad Road has a broad range of hotels and restaurants.
A Delhi day trip is possible, but an overnight stay creates a safer schedule buffer.

hiddenGems: Mughal Heritage Walk - A community-linked route through Kachhpura with river and monument views; arrange through a responsible current operator.
Roman Catholic Cemetery - An unusual historic cemetery with monuments reflecting Agra's international connections.
Gyarah Sidi - Riverside remains associated with astronomical observation, best approached with local guidance.
Korai Village - A rural cultural visit near Fatehpur Sikri; choose an ethical community-based experience.
Soami Bagh - An elaborate, still-evolving marble memorial complex in Dayalbagh; observe visitor and photography rules.
Bateshwar - A temple town on the Yamuna suited to travellers with extra time and reliable transport.

faq.question: Is one day enough for Agra?
faq.answer: One long day covers the Taj Mahal and Agra Fort. An overnight stay adds weather flexibility and time for the smaller Mughal sites.

faq.question: When is the Taj Mahal closed?
faq.answer: It is generally closed to tourists on Fridays. Rules can change, so verify on the official ticketing or monument website before travel.

faq.question: Is sunrise always the best Taj Mahal visit?
faq.answer: Sunrise often means cooler temperatures and fewer crowds, but winter fog can hide views. Late afternoon can be a better backup.

faq.question: How do I avoid shopping scams in Agra?
faq.answer: Decline unrequested shop stops, use licensed guides, compare prices and insist on clear documentation for expensive purchases.
